_comment: Shared fixture for the TWO trade-grading implementations (math audit
* frontend/lib/league-analysis.js  -> private /trades page
* src/public_league/trade_grading.py -> public /league timeline
Asserted by tests/public_league/test_trade_grade_parity.py and
frontend/__tests__/trade-grade-parity.test.js.  NEITHER half may
hardcode an expectation of its own: if the two drift, exactly one
suite goes red against a shared, human-authored statement of intent.
Every number in 'bands', 'bandCases' and 'tradeCases' is hand-derived
from the formula, not captured from either implementation:
netAdjusted  = sum(got) - sum(gave) + vaNet
gotEffective = sum(got)  + max(0,  vaNet)
gaveEffective= sum(gave) + max(0, -vaNet)
pctGap       = netAdjusted / max(gotEffective, gaveEffective, 1) * 100
and pctGap is bucketed by |pctGap| through the 'bands' table below.
'vaEngineCases' is the one section whose expectations come from
outside this repo: they are real keeptradecut.com trade-calculator
captures (scripts/ktc_va_observations.json, captured 2026-04-25), so
both implementations are pinned to KTC itself rather than to each
other.  The tolerance absorbs KTC's iterative solver converging
slightly differently in a browser than in Node or CPython.

bands.why: Cut points shared by both implementations. Each entry is the LOWEST |pctGap| that lands in that band; the band below owns everything under it.

bandCases.why: Identical sides: zero net, zero pct, fair on both ends.
bandCases.label: Fair trade

bandCases.why: 300/10000 = 3.00% — the edge belongs to the band above, so this is a Slight win, not a Fair trade. Same letter, different label.
bandCases.label: Slight win

bandCases.why: Finding C3's headline case. 1000/10000 = 10.0% linear -> Good win (A-). The retired public formula raised each asset to 1.65 first, scoring the same trade at 1 - 0.9^1.65 = 15.95% -> Clear win (B+): a full band higher off the same two numbers.
bandCases.label: Good win

bandCases.why: 2500/10000 = 25.00% — the winner ladder tops out here.
bandCases.label: Big win

bandCases.why: -300/10000 = -3.00%. Denominator is the LARGER effective side, which is now the one they gave up.
bandCases.label: Slight overpay

bandCases.why: Losing mirror of ten-pct-linear-edge: -10.0% -> Overpay (B), where the alpha formula said Bad deal (C).
bandCases.label: Overpay

bandCases.why: -4000/10000 = -40.00% — the loser ladder tops out here.
bandCases.label: Fleeced

bandCases.why: Linear net is zero; a +2000 VA makes it a 2000/10000 = 20% win. The VA also widens the denominator, which is why this is 20% and not 25%.
bandCases.label: Clear win

bandCases.why: Mirror: -2000 VA on a linear-even trade, denominator 8000 + 2000 on the gave side.
bandCases.label: Bad deal

bandCases.why: +1000 linear but -1500 VA: they took the pile and gave the stud. netAdjusted -500 over max(9000, 9500) = -5.26%, an overpay despite winning on raw sums.
bandCases.label: Slight overpay

bandCases.why: 3000/7000 = 42.857%, NOT 3000/6000 = 50%: the +1000 VA is added to the got side before the max.
bandCases.label: Big win

bandCases.why: Nothing on either side resolved to a value. The scale floor of 1 keeps this at 0% instead of dividing by zero.
bandCases.label: Fair trade

bandCases.why: A 0.5-value asset for nothing. The floor of 1 in the denominator caps this at 50%, not 100% — pins that both halves floor the SCALE and not the values.
bandCases.label: Big win

bandCases.why: 6000 of pieces for 6000 of pieces is fair. Under the retired alpha formula the concentrated side would have scored far ahead.
bandCases.label: Fair trade

tradeCases.why: Finding C3 end to end. KTC suppresses the VA on any 1-for-1 package, so both sides are plain ratios: +10.0% / -10.0%.

Three-way where sent and received pools do not pair up. Every side is 1-for-1 so the VA stays suppressed. Team C receives the SECOND-smallest pile (3000) yet is a clear winner because it only sent 1000 — ranking sides by received total would have called it the unremarkable middle and stamped it Fair.
A side with an empty got list. The VA engine returns 0 whenever either package is empty, so this is a clean +/-100%.

Both halves must discard the same garbage before summing: null, negatives, zero, and non-numeric strings all vanish, leaving a 1000-for-1000 swap. If either half let one through as a NaN, every band comparison against it would be false and the side would fall out the bottom as Fleeced.
tradeCases.activityWhy: This case states what the ARITHMETIC does with an unusable number, and both halves still agree on that. It is NOT what the public activity feed does with an unusable ASSET: there, null / non-numeric is the valuation callable saying it could not price the asset, and since 2026-08-05 (W19-F003) the feed withholds the letter rather than grading the remaining subset. So the activity replay of this one case asserts the abstention instead of the letter. The two are consistent — grade_trade_side is still handed exactly the sanitized numbers below — and stating the divergence here keeps it deliberate rather than a drift nobody noticed.

vaEngineCases.why: The signed VA one team's got-vs-gave equation earns. Expectations are real keeptradecut.com trade-calculator captures, NOT output of either implementation: scripts/ktc_va_observations.json, capturedAt 2026-04-25, one entry per topology. vaNet is KTC's valueAdjustmentTeam1 minus valueAdjustmentTeam2 with got as team1.

cases.why: 1v1 control — KTC never displays a VA on a one-for-one.
Solo strong vs two mids: the consolidating side earns the premium.
Elite single asset against three mid pieces — the largest premium shape.
Intensity-balanced 2v2: KTC suppresses the badge entirely.
2v2 with the studs stacked on one side — fires despite equal counts.
3v3 where the best and worst pieces sit on different sides.
3v3 firing on the OTHER side — pins the sign convention, not just the magnitude.
Deep even-count package that still earns a premium.
